lead: A variable is a name stuck onto a value. Assignment creates the name: price = 45 makes the name price point to the value 45. Python needs no type declaration. The same name can hold an integer now and a string later; this is dynamic typing. The name itself must follow fixed rules. It may use letters, digits and underscore, but it cannot start with a digit, cannot contain a space or hyphen, cannot be a keyword, and is case sensitive. These rules keep names readable and stop clashes with Python's own words.
prereq: You need: 1.3, interactive and script mode, where names live while the file runs.

blocks.text: An assignment has a left side (a name) and a right side (an expression). Python evaluates the right side first, then binds the name to that value. price = 45 evaluates 45, then binds price to 45 (rupees). qty = 3 binds qty to 3 (items). bill = price * qty evaluates 45 × 3 = 135, then binds bill to 135 (rupees). No separate declaration line is needed. The first assignment is the declaration.

Python is dynamically typed. x = 10 makes x hold an integer. x = "ten" rebinds the same name x to a string. The old integer is unchanged; x now points to a new value. The type belongs to the value, not to the name. What a name may hold is covered in 1.5.

Multiple assignment binds several names in one line. x = y = 5 binds x to 5 and y to 5. The swap a, b = b, a evaluates the right side as a pair first, then rebinds the names; it needs no temporary variable. del removes a name: del x makes x unknown until a new assignment. Scope and lifetime are in Unit 2; mutability and object identity are in Unit 3.
Use snake_case for ordinary names: total_marks, unit_price, student_count. Lowercase words joined by underscores read well.
An identifier is a name you give to a variable, function, class or module. The rules are fixed.

items: Allowed characters are a–z, A–Z, 0–9 and underscore _.
The first character cannot be a digit. _temp is valid; 2nd_rank is not.
Spaces and hyphens are not allowed. my-var is invalid; my_var is valid.
Case matters. Total and total are two different names. Price and price are different.
A keyword cannot be used as an identifier. class is a keyword; class_ is not.

blocks.text: An identifier may contain digits after the first character: roll_no_2 is valid. Keywords are words Python reserves for its own syntax; some syllabi call them reserved words. Common keywords are: False, None, True, and, as, assert, break, class, continue, def, del, elif, else, except, finally, for, from, global, if, import, in, is, lambda, not, or, pass, raise, return, try, while, with, yield. The exact set changes with the Python version. help('keywords') prints the set for your interpreter. If a name is not a keyword and follows the character rules, it is legal.

A name has no value before its first assignment. If you print total before total = 0, Python raises NameError: name 'total' is not defined. It does not use 0, a blank string or any default. The error names the missing identifier. To fix it, assign a value first. NameError is a runtime error; see 1.8 for error families.

A keyword used as a name gives SyntaxError at the point Python parses the line, before any assignment runs. For example class = 10 is invalid; use class_name = 10. Case slips create a NameError too: Total = 10 then print(total) fails because Total and total differ. A hyphen creates SyntaxError: my-var = 5 is read as my minus var.

examples.question: Which of these are valid Python identifiers: total_marks, 2nd_rank, _temp, my-var, class, Price? Then run price = 45, qty = 3, bill = price * qty and state the value of bill.
steps: total_marks: starts with letter t; contains letters and underscore; not a keyword. Valid.
2nd_rank: first character is digit 2; not allowed. Invalid.
_temp: first character is underscore; allowed. Valid.
my-var: contains hyphen -; not allowed. Invalid.
class: keyword; not allowed as an identifier. Invalid.
Price: starts with uppercase P; allowed; case sensitive, so Price differs from price. Valid.
bill = price * qty: 45 × 3 = 135; binds bill to 135 rupees.
examples.answer: Valid identifiers are total_marks, _temp and Price; invalid are 2nd_rank, my-var and class; bill holds 135.
examples.check:
price = 45
qty = 3
bill = price * qty
print(bill)

code.code:
price = 45
qty = 3
bill = price * qty
print(bill)

traps: A name has no value before its first assignment. Printing it raises NameError; it does not quietly hold 0 or an empty string.
A keyword is never an identifier. class = 10 fails, but class_name = 10 works.
Case matters: Total, total and TOTAL are three different names. print(total) after Total = 10 raises NameError.
A hyphen is subtraction, not part of a name. my-var = 5 is read as my minus var; use my_var.
Dynamic typing rebinds the name, not the old value. x = 10 then x = "ten" leaves the integer 10 unchanged; x now points to a string.

quiz.q: List three rules that a Python identifier must follow.
quiz.a: It may use letters, digits and underscore; it cannot start with a digit; it cannot be a keyword; it cannot contain spaces or hyphens. Any three.

quiz.q: Why is x = 10 followed by x = "ten" allowed in Python?
quiz.a: Python is dynamically typed. The first line binds x to an integer value. The second line rebinds the same name x to a string value. The type belongs to the value, not to the name.

quiz.q: Which are valid identifiers: _count, 9lives, total-price, for, Value? Explain each.
quiz.a: _count valid: starts with underscore. 9lives invalid: starts with digit. total-price invalid: contains hyphen. for invalid: keyword. Value valid: starts with a letter; uppercase is allowed.

quiz.q: A student writes Total = 50 then print(total). What happens and why? Give one fix.
quiz.a: Python raises NameError because names are case sensitive. Total and total are different names, and total has no binding. Fix: print(Total), or write total = 50 in the first line.

quiz.q: After a = 7; b = 3; a, b = b, a, what are a and b? Show the intermediate pair.
quiz.a: The right side b, a is evaluated first as (3, 7). Then a is bound to 3 and b is bound to 7. Final: a = 3, b = 7.

quiz.q: What does del price do? What happens if price is printed immediately afterwards?
quiz.a: del price removes the binding of the name price. Printing price afterwards raises NameError until a new assignment gives price a value.

quiz.q: Write one assignment line that binds x and y to 5.

quiz.a: Any four from: False, None, True, and, as, assert, break, class, continue, def, del, elif, else, except, finally, for, from, global, if, import, in, is, lambda, not, or, pass, raise, return, try, while, with, yield.

beyond: Not for the exam. In real code, names act as documentation; linters such as pycodestyle flag bad names. Refactoring tools rename a variable across a project by finding its binding. help('keywords') is a quick check in a new Python version. Search next for PEP 8 naming conventions, NameError traceback, and Python's LEGB rule.
